summary: Wes Borton specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at East Carolina University, under Derek F. Maher, and at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at International Christian University and Harvard University (Ph.D. ~1970–1975), he taught at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and was a professor at UC Davis (~1978–2008).

Whitelaw Ainslie worked in Indology and other fields. He served as an assistant surgeon (1788) and surgeon (1794–1815) for the East India Company, and became a Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh in 1829.
Whitley Stokes was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St Columba's College and Trinity College Dublin (B.A. 1846–1851). He also studied under Carl Siegfried and Rudolf Thomas Siegfried.

Whitney Cox works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago (PhD 1998–2006) under Sheldon Pollock and others, he held posts at SOAS (~2006–2013) and the University of Chicago (~2001–2006; Professor ~2013).

Widi Widiyanto specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned degrees from Sekolah Tinggi Agama Buddha Maha Prajna and a doctorate from Universitas Hindu Indonesia (2022–2025), and became a Dosen Tetap at STIAB Jinarakkhita in 2022.

Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at the University of Ceylon and earning a PhD from SOAS/University of London (~1953–1956). He held posts at the University of Ceylon, University of Peradeniya, and University of Kelaniya.

Wiktor Jan Porzeziński was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Moscow State University under Filipp Fortunatov. He served as Privatdozent at Moscow State University (1903–1921) and as professor at the University of Warsaw and Catholic University of Lublin.
Wilber Theodore Elmore was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (~1913–1915) and taught at Palmer Theological Seminary in 1925.

Wilbur Stone Deming worked in Indology and religious studies after studying at Brown University and Boston University. He was a member of the American Marathi Mission from 1912 and superintendent of the American Mission High School, Ahmednagar, in 1924.

Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He completed a master's program at the University of Colorado Boulder and studied at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith was a religious studies scholar educated at Toronto, Cambridge, and Princeton. He held major posts at Forman Christian College, McGill University, and Harvard University, where he directed the Center for the Study of World Religions (~1964–1973).

Wilfred Harvey Schoff worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania. He served at the Philadelphia Commercial Museum (1900) and was a visiting lecturer at UW-Madison (1901) and the University of Illinois (1903).

Wilfrid Sellars was a philosopher who studied at the University of Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the Universities of Iowa and Minnesota, Yale University, and held a professorship at the University of Pittsburgh from 1963 to 1989.
Wilfried Nölle was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen from 1946 to 1950, where he was a student of Helmuth von Glasenapp (~1947–1950).

Wilhelm Alexander Unkrig was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kazan Theological Academy. He served as a librarian at the Anthropos Institute and Leiden University, and lectured in Tibetan and Mongolian at Goethe University Frankfurt (1943).

Wilhelm Brandenstein was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Innsbruck and Vienna under scholars including Paul Kretschmer and Nikolai Trubetzkoy. He spent his academic career at the University of Graz, directing its Institute for Comparative Linguistics from 1941 to 1967.

Wilhelm Cartellieri was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig and under Georg Bühler at the University of Vienna (Ph.D. 1878–1884). He completed his habilitation (1899) and was appointed associate professor (1902) at the University of Innsbruck.

Wilhelm Deecke was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He served as an educator and director at Ernestinenschule, Gymnasium Jean Sturm, Collège de Bouxwiller, and Lycée Albert-Schweitzer Mulhouse.
Wilhelm Dilger worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as a missionary with the Basel Mission from 1880 to 1907 and held a post at the University of Tübingen in 1910.
